notes:
User is planning another backyard BBQ for friends and wants to try new recipes. Menu is expanding to include low-and-slow smoked brisket, pulled-pork sandwiches with coleslaw and pickles, ribs, mac and cheese (a user favorite), burgers, hot dogs, and grilled pineapple. A friend named Emily previously brought grilled pineapple to the user’s birthday party, inspiring this idea. The user has a new Weber gas grill that they love for quick weeknight dinners.

Preferred brisket approach: 10–12 lb whole brisket, smoker at 225°F/110°C, trimmed and with silver skin removed, optional yellow mustard binder, even coat of rub (previously discussed Killer Hogs BBQ Rub), and post oak for classic Texas-style smoke. Place fat-side up, monitor temperature/airflow, add wood as needed, optionally use a water pan, wrap after bark sets and around 160°F, then cook to roughly 190–205°F or probe-tender, judging doneness by thermometer rather than time. Rest before slicing.

The user enjoys practical, detailed BBQ guidance and has asked about wood, rubs, smoker setup, sides, burgers, hot dogs, pineapple, and sauces. Smoker type and wood-chip/chunk capacity are still unknown.

Pulled pork: serve on a bun with coleslaw and pickles. Suggested boneless pork shoulder/Boston butt, dry rub, smoke at 225–250°F until about 190–195°F, rest 30–60 minutes, then shred. Mild wood choices include apple, cherry, hickory (sparingly), and pecan. Potential flavor additions include bacon/sausage/butter and sauce during the final hour.

BBQ sauce preference has changed/expanded: the current favorite is Kansas City Masterpiece BBQ sauce, especially for ribs and pulled pork, though they are open to trying Sweet Baby Ray’s, Franklin, Bone Suckin’, Stubb’s, or Dinosaur Bar-B-Que. Sweet Baby Ray’s was previously planned for ribs and as a possible brisket finishing sauce. Offer multiple sauces for guests and consider using sauce as a final glaze rather than heavily coating meat.

Other menu ideas discussed: tangy creamy coleslaw to balance rich brisket; baked beans; grilled vegetables; cornebread; potato salad. Grilled pineapple should be ripe, sweet, and firm (Hawaiian Gold/Smooth Cayenne suggested), cut into wedges/slices, lightly oiled, seasoned, and grilled over medium-high heat (375–400°F) until caramelized
